name: National Assembly
description: Serbia’s domed parliament building, finished in 1936. Protesters stormed it on 5 October 2000, bringing down Milošević.

name: Belgrade Fortress (Kalemegdan)
description: The old fortress on the ridge where the Sava meets the Danube, now a large park with walls, gates and river views.

name: House of Flowers
description: Tito’s mausoleum, a winter garden where he and his wife are buried, part of the Museum of Yugoslavia.

name: Slavija Square
description: A large roundabout square at the south end of the centre, where several main streets meet.

name: Western City Gate (Genex Tower)
description: A Brutalist pair of towers from 1977–80 at the entrance to New Belgrade, linked by a bridge with a round restaurant on top.

name: Former Chinese embassy site
places: Chinese Cultural Centre (site of 1999 embassy bombing)
description: The site of the Chinese embassy that NATO bombed in May 1999, killing three people. A Chinese cultural centre now stands there.

name: Nikola Tesla Museum
description: A museum of Tesla’s papers, inventions and working models, in a villa in the centre. His ashes are kept there in a gilded sphere.

name: Red Star Stadium
description: Red Star Belgrade’s football stadium, nicknamed the Marakana, and the biggest stadium in Serbia.
